name: After Effects Text Animation Preset Stack
use_when: A high-quality Reel needs repeatable text entrances, typewriter reveals, highlights, glow, shadow, or subtle texture.
The agent is building a brand's reusable After Effects text language.
Text animation needs to sync tightly with spoken words in a vertical short.
A scripted animation has been sketched and needs typewriter, Trim Paths, glow, or shape/text reveals.
avoid_when: Plain captions are enough and extra text motion would slow comprehension.
The project has serious or sensitive tone where flashy text would feel wrong.
The preset has not been tested on the actual font, text length, and phone-size layout.

timeline_pattern.pattern: create_text -> center_anchor -> choose_font_weight -> animate_position_or_text_animator -> easy_ease_or_range_shape -> add_shadow_glow_texture -> save_preset -> disable_heavy_effects_if_lag -> enable_before_render
timeline_pattern.typewriter_rule: For smoother typewriter text, use Text Animator with ramp-up shape and offset keyframes from -100 to 100 rather than a harsh character reveal.
timeline_pattern.preset_rule: Save presets by behavior, such as smooth typewriter, slide up, slide out, glow shadow, or turbulent texture.
timeline_pattern.heavy_effect_rule: Disable heavy effects while editing if After Effects lags, then turn them on before final render.
timeline_pattern.sketch_rule: Build text, shapes, and pen paths from a sketch before polishing animation details.

motion.rule: Text should enter on or just before the spoken word it represents, with keyframes shaped for flow instead of linear motion.

keyframe_values.opacity_before_position: For position+opacity entrances, opacity can start slightly before the final position keyframe so the element appears naturally.
keyframe_values.smooth_typewriter_offset: Offset -100 to 100 with ramp-up shape is a useful smooth typewriter setup.
keyframe_values.turbulent_displace: Subtle text texture can start around Amount 10-15 and Size 6-8; animate Random Seed with an expression like time*8 when appropriate.
keyframe_values.highlight: Use Trim Paths from 0 to 100 on a line/highlight and ease the keyframes.

sound.rule: Pair typewriter, slide, highlight, or glow moments with SFX only when the text motion is a real beat.

captions.rule: Do not duplicate animated text with captions unless the duplicate is needed for accessibility or comprehension.

color.rule: Text glow, shadow, and gradient should improve readability while staying inside the brand palette.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use drawtext enable expressions, alpha fades, and pre-rendered text assets for approximations; complex text animator behavior should be rendered from AE/Remotion.
implementation.remotion: Create text animation presets with props for mode, startFrame, duration, easing, blur, opacity, translate, typewriterProgress, turbulence, and highlightProgress.
implementation.blender: Use text objects and animation curves for spatial text, but keep social subtitle readability rules.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use reusable text animations sparingly and verify that typewriter/slide presets line up with speech.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use After Effects text animators and animation presets, or Premiere Essential Graphics for simpler slide/fade/pop text. For diagram-like ideas, sketch the shape/text layout before building the animation.

common_mistakes: Animating every word instead of the words that carry meaning.
Saving presets with vague names that cannot be reused safely.
Leaving turbulent/glow effects so strong that the text becomes noisy.
Forgetting to turn disabled effects back on before render.
Letting text animation finish after the spoken word has passed.
Building a complex text animation before the sketch or voiceover order is clear.
qc: Text appears in sync with the spoken word or concept.
Preset names describe behavior and can be reused safely.
Glow, shadow, gradient, and turbulence preserve readability at phone size.
Heavy effects are enabled before final render.
Animated text does not duplicate captions unnecessarily.
The animation follows the sketched reveal order and voiceover timing.
